is_anopheles.evidence: The study collected and evaluated Anopheles gambiae s.l. (specifically An. coluzzii and An. arabiensis) in IDP camps in Maiduguri, Nigeria (p. 3, 5, 7).

reports_target_markers.evidence: No insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped in this study. The authors only mention vgsc-995F and vgsc-1570Y frequencies in the study site description (p. 3) by citing an unpublished paper under review ('Allan R, Scherrer R, Estecha-Querol S, Weetman D, Paris L, Ba'abba Goni U, et al, The effectiveness of long-lasting spatial repellent against malaria in humanitarian crisis settings in Northern Nigeria. Lancet Infectious Diseases. 2025, under review').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts or frequencies generated by this study are reported. Molecular work in this paper was strictly limited to species identification (PCR/qPCR for An. gambiae complex and sequencing of COI/ITS2) (p. 5).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Sabon Gari and Doro internally displaced persons (IDP) camps in Maiduguri, Borno State, Nigeria between 2024 and 2025 (p. 3-4).

is_primary_study.evidence: While this is a primary field trial evaluating ATSB entomological efficacy, it does not conduct primary investigation or report original data for insecticide resistance markers (it cites another work under review for resistance marker frequencies) (p. 3).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study took place in Sabon Gari (11°50'50.4"N 13°06'32.0"E) and Doro (11°52'51.1"N 13°07'00.8"E) IDP camps in Maiduguri LGA, Borno State, Nigeria (p. 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field trials and mosquito collections were carried out between July 2024 and March 2025 (p. 4-5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: New empirical field trial of ATSBs in Maiduguri, Nigeria.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary tables cover demographic, remote sensing, and species density/larval count data; no resistance marker genotyping was performed.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the entomological impact of attractive targeted sugar baits (ATSB) on mosquito vector densities (Anopheles gambiae s.l., Aedes aegypti, Culex spp.) in two IDP camps in Maiduguri, Borno State, Nigeria. Molecular analysis was restricted to species identification; no insecticide resistance markers were genotyped.
exclusion_reasons: Does not genotype any target insecticide-resistance markers; reference to vgsc mutations is merely cited from another study under review.
No extractable resistance marker genotype data reported.
